transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, too. Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, honestly. It's probably nothing major. But... I guess what made me come in is that, just for the past year or so, I've been getting a little sidetracked. 

I mean, I run a company, so there's always a lot going on, right? That's normal. But lately, it's like the absolute smallest things—just a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office, or even a random thought popping into my head about my in-laws—it just pulls me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. I still get things done, of course, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. But... I don't know, does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing people usually come to see you for?
Looking back at your life, did you experience these same types of struggles with staying focused or being easily distracted when you were a child or teenager?

Well, um... yeah, I suppose so. I mean, I was always just a really energetic kid, you know? Just full of ideas, nothing too crazy. But, looking back... yeah, I guess it was around then, too. 

My teachers were actually always moving my seat around. I guess I talked a little too much? And, um, I'd get up without asking sometimes, or I'd kind of... blurt things out before they even finished asking the question. I think I was just really eager to participate, you know? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker. I mean, boys will be boys, right? Is that the sort of thing you're asking about?
Do you still find yourself feeling physically restless or having a hard time sitting still in meetings or during quiet activities?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's a huge problem, really. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or being disruptive! But... I guess, yeah, when I'm really supposed to just sit quietly—like at longer family dinners, or, um, during the volunteer meetings I help out with at church—it can be a little tough. 

It kind of feels like there's this... this motor running inside me? Like I just need to move a little bit, or at least do something with my hands. I usually just fiddle with a pen or fold a napkin so I don't bother anybody else. I mean, I'm a guy who likes to get things done and stay busy, so sitting around can just feel a bit unproductive, you know? I hope that doesn't sound too strange. Is that the kind of restlessness you're talking about?
When you have these urges to move or fidget in meetings, do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are speaking or finishing their sentences for them?

Well, um... I really try not to be rude, I promise. I know how important it is to listen. But... I guess, lately, yeah, I might be doing that a little bit. 

It's just that my brain moves so fast, and I kind of already know where they're going with it, so I just... help them get there? Like, if an employee is explaining something, I might just finish their thought for them to keep things moving. Or, um, with my wife, if she's talking to her parents, I'll just sort of jump right in. I don't mean anything by it at all! Just trying to be involved. But... I can kind of tell it rubs people the wrong way sometimes. They get this look on their face. I really don't want to be that guy who talks over everyone. Does that make sense? I hope that's not too terrible of a thing to admit.

Looking at your professional and personal life, would you say these difficulties with focus and impulsivity are currently causing you significant problems, or do you feel you are still managing them well enough?

Well, um... I really wouldn't say things are falling apart or anything like that. I'm definitely still keeping up overall, you know? I work really hard to make sure everything gets done. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it is starting to cause a few hiccups. 

I just... I worry that I'm losing a little bit of trust at home, maybe? Like when family plans get a bit derailed because I jumped the gun or wasn't really tuned in. And at work, I can kind of sense that my employees are losing a little patience with me. Especially during mentoring conversations or meetings when I, you know, step on their toes or don't let things go the way they probably should. 

I really do try my best to be a good boss and a good husband, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm failing at everything. I'm just noticing that these little things are... adding up a bit more than I'd like. Is that the kind of problem you were asking about? I hope it's okay that I shared that.

Between your difficulties with focus and your struggles with restlessness and impulsivity, which of these two areas would you say has been the more persistent or bothersome challenge for you throughout your life?

Well, um... I guess if I had to pick, the restlessness and the jumping in too fast is probably the one that's been around the longest. I really don't want to sound like I've been a problem my whole life, but... yeah, that part has always been there. 

Looking back, it was kind of like this when I was a kid, too. I mean, I wasn't a bad kid, I promise! Just... very enthusiastic, maybe? My teachers were always moving my seat because I talked a bit too much, or I'd get up without asking. And I'd always just blurt things out before they even finished asking the question. I just got so excited to answer, you know? I really didn't mean to be disruptive. It's just always been a bit harder for me to hold back that... that energy, I guess. I hope that makes sense. Is it normal for it to start that early?
